tree_commit_note: the commit that CONTAINS the measured code, golds and ranking, verified by tests/retrieve-baseline-provenance.test.mjs. Supersedes 70c65eb, which predates the vendored-source prune (2c3376f) and the bge query-instruction fix (33d780e).

code.bar_note: SPEC BAR 0.80 NOT MET. Measured 0.40 (baseline before this change 0.30). The gain is one general fix: bge-*-en-v1.x is trained asymmetrically, the document side is embedded as '<title>\n<body>' and query() was sending the bare string, so the two sides of the comparison were formatted as the model does not expect. encode_query() adds the model's retrieval instruction on the QUERY side only (never the build side, which would need a rebuild). Ablation: prompt OFF = 0.30, prompt ON = 0.40, so the entire gain is this fix. Identifier-aware tokenization ships in the same commit but is measured inert on both metrics. FIVE alternatives were implemented, measured and REJECTED: a lexical candidate pass, coverage-as-ranking-term, canonical-source bonus, transcript demotion and echo demotion took the slice to 0.30 and dropped held-out natural-language probes from 2/5 to 0/5. CEILING: a paraphrased question can have zero token overlap with its own answer -- bin/lib/journal.mjs contains none of {strong, weak, verdict} for 'which module decides strong versus weak trust verdicts', it says 'Single-writer by construction' -- so no lexical weight can rank it (COV_WEIGHT 0.5/1.5/3.0 all measured code=0.30, held-out 1/5). The remaining gap requires a retrieval-model change: stronger embeddings, an FTS5/BM25 index, or code-aware chunking so a card body contains the identifiers a question names. Not ranking constants. MEASUREMENT HAZARD: ~/.heimdall/global.db is LIVE and the reconciler indexed the agent's own session files during this work (402,993 -> 403,000 cards), which moved an identical tree between 0.30 and 0.40. Pin the index before any before/after comparison.

fact.bar_note: First measured-reachable bar. Reached 0.90 with queries drawn from the MIDDLE of each gold, after review showed the first version used each gold's own opening words, which is a rigged benchmark.

person.bar_note: First measured-reachable bar. Reached 1.00. The original 0.00 was structural: 0 of 10 queries named their own gold and 3 of 10 golds were absent from people.db.

regressions.default_kb_search_output: byte-identical to a golden captured before the change; tests/kinds-default-identical.test.mjs passes and tests/fixtures/kb-search-default.golden is unchanged in git (git diff --exit-code)
regressions.code_slice_vs_0.30_spec_bar: MET: 0.40 >= 0.30, verified after the global.db rebuild. The gap that existed at merge time was environmental, proven by the pre-Phase-1 commit measuring 0.10 on the same index.

review: four adversarial rounds in Phase 3, one in Phase 4; this run fixed 2 BLOCKERs and 5 MAJORs before the measurement
gold_set_note: Person and fact gold sets were rebuilt in Phase 4. As shipped in Phase 0, 0 of 10 person queries named their own gold and 0 of 10 fact golds existed anywhere in the corpus, so both 0.00s measured the gold set rather than retrieval. Every replacement gold is a real record verified present in people.db / journal.db before use; fact queries draw from the middle of the gold, not its opening, and a test asserts gold/query token overlap so a rigged set fails the build.
generalization_probe: Held-out natural-language probes (5 questions written as questions, never drawn from the gold set) are the only signal that did not lie during this work: the ten gold rows moved 0.30 -> 0.50 -> 0.30 across five successive 'improvements' while held-out recall went 2/5 -> 0/5 -> 1/5. Every change shipped here was required to hold or improve BOTH metrics. The shipped fix holds held-out at 2/5 while moving the gold rows 0.30 -> 0.40.
